links.note: English churchmen helped lead the Frankish reform from the start. In 742 Carloman, a ruler of the Franks, set the English missionary Boniface as archbishop over the bishops of his realm. Alcuin of York later wrote that he had come to Francia to help King Charles in the Catholic faith.

links.note: In the ninth century a forger in the Frankish lands made a collection of fake early papal letters, the False Decretals. In 1081 Pope Gregory VII quoted one of them, a letter said to be from Pope Julius, to argue that Rome could judge earthly rulers. His modern editor traced that letter to the forged collection.

links.note: Kievan Rus' took its Christian books and its letters from the Cyril and Methodius mission. Mouravieff, a Russian church historian writing in 1838, says the brothers' Slavonic Bible later helped win the Russians to the faith. Herberstein retold the Rus' annals in 1549. He says the Rus' began to write down their past once the Slavonic letters came.

sources.work: A. N. Mouravieff, A History of the Church of Russia (1838), trans. R. W. Blackmore (Oxford, 1842); vendored at cic/texts/mouravieff_history-of-the-church-of-russia_blackmore1842.txt: the brothers' translation 'became afterwards a most blessed instrument for the conversion of the Russians'

Robert Pinkerton, note in Platon, The Present State of the Greek Church in Russia (Edinburgh, 1814): the Slavonic Bible 'made in the ninth century, by two learned Greeks, Cyril and Methodius'; 'The present version in use among the Russians is that of Ostrog'

Sigmund von Herberstein, Notes upon Russia (Rerum Moscoviticarum Commentarii, 1549), trans. R. H. Major (1851), vol. I: a sixteenth-century retelling of the Rus' annals, used here as a later account, not as a primary for the ninth century: the Rus' annals 'began to be written and recorded' after Michael 'had sent the Sclavonian characters into Bulgaria' (which the same passage dates [898])

links.from_name: The Byzantine Imperial Church (Heraclian & Iconoclast Eras)
links.note: In 754 a council called by the emperor Constantine V banned holy images. At its close the bishops cursed John of Damascus as a teacher of impiety, calling him by his family name, Mansur. Later historians write that the emperor then pressed the monks to obey. Many fled, they say, and some were killed.

links.note: After 843 the empress Theodora had the Paulicians hunted, and the patriarch Photius wrote against them. Peter of Sicily, sent to Tephrike by Basil I, wrote a book against them to warn the new church in Bulgaria. In 970 John Tzimiskes moved Paulicians from Asia to Plovdiv.

links.note: Peter of Sicily, a Byzantine envoy at Tephrike around 870, wrote that the Paulicians meant to send preachers to Bulgaria. Older historians, and some modern ones, built a line from them to the Bogomils on reports like this. Others point out that the Armenian sources show no dualism, and doubt the line. No Paulician or Bogomil text settles it.

links.from_name: The Church of the East under the Abbasids
links.note: Around 800 the head of the church, Timothy, named the Indians among the peoples in his care. In the 850s a later head, Theodosius, made a church law for the far-off metropolitans, India's among them. Each was to write to the patriarch every six years. Mingana read the bishop's name on the Kollam copper plates as Sabrisho.
